typescript.reason: tsc -b passes on 7.0.2, but typescript-eslint refuses to load against it ("typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0", peer range >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, tracking issue typescript-eslint#10940), so npm run check cannot lint. TS 6.0.x is inside that peer range and is the realistic next step; revisit when typescript-eslint ships TS >=7.1 support.

_note_three: three 0.185.1 and @types/three 0.185.4 landed on 2026-09-04 without the desktop verification round their deferrals were waiting on -- an explicit maintainer decision to take the upgrade first and pay the verification debt afterwards. The outstanding check is tracked in docs/VRM_VRMA_COMPATIBILITY.md and docs/DECISIONS.md (2026-09-04 entry), not here: a deferral means 'reviewed, not installed', and these are installed. Do not re-add them here to represent the pending check.

@types/node.reason: Node type definitions track the runtime the project builds on, not the newest published. CI runs Node 24 and package.json requires >=24; typing against Node 26 would surface APIs the build environment does not have. Re-confirmed 2026-08-29 against 26.4.0: the reasoning is unchanged, only the version the deferral is pinned to.

electron.reason: Electron 44 is a major. This repo requires the release notes, npm run check, and a real Windows run of the packaged app before a major lands, and the packaged-app half cannot be judged from CI: the avatar, VRM/VRMA playback and the tray/DPI behaviour only show up on a real desktop. npm run check passes on 43.4.1; this is verification debt, not a known incompatibility. Pair it with the same desktop verification round that three.js is waiting on.
